_comment: WORKFLOWS — how a feature actually gets executed.
WHY THESE ARE TEMPLATES AND NOT SIXTY-EIGHT COPIES.
The brief asks that every feature have a workflow. It also asks, twice,
that this not become a huge amount of duplicated code. Both are satisfied
the same way the site's own components are: the SHAPE of the work is
shared and the CONTENT of the work is not.
A logo, a business card and an ad design move through the same five
stages — brief, make, check ourselves, check with the client, release —
and differ entirely in what is made, with what, and what makes it good.
So the stages live here, once, and the specifics live on the feature:
`inputs`, `executionSteps`, `tools`, `outputs`, `deliverables`,
`qualityChecks`, `completionCriteria`, `revisionRules`.
tools/build-catalogue.js MATERIALISES the two into one object per
feature, with a real `workflow_id` and `feature_id`, resolving the
$feature.* tokens below. That materialised set — one full workflow per
feature, the exact shape the brief specifies — is what an automation, a
project board or an agent consumes. Nothing here is authored twice and
nothing here reaches a browser.
A feature may override any stage by declaring `workflowOverrides`.
TOKENS resolved at materialisation:
$feature.inputs $feature.executionSteps $feature.tools
$feature.outputs $feature.deliverables $feature.qualityChecks
$feature.completionCriteria $feature.revisionRules.rounds
$feature.name.en $feature.dependencies.requires

wf.design_concept.label: Original design work, where the first question is which direction to take
wf.design_concept.trigger: Scope signed and the stage's prerequisites are satisfied.
prerequisites: A completed brief from the client

stages.objective: Turn the client's material into a written direction before anything is drawn.
actions: Read every supplied input.
Write the direction in one paragraph.
Send it and get it agreed in words.
stages.validation: The client has responded to the direction, not merely received it.

stages.objective: Produce genuinely distinct options.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: No two concepts are the same idea in different colours.

stages.objective: Show the work in the context it will live in.
actions: Present in context, never floating on white.
State what each concept is arguing, in one line.
Ask for a decision, not for an opinion.
stages.validation: The client has chosen one, in writing.

stages.objective: Take the chosen concept to final within the agreed rounds.
actions: Apply comments.
Count the round.
Stop at the limit and quote further work rather than absorbing it.
stages.validation: Rounds used are within $feature.revisionRules.rounds.

stages.objective: Produce and deliver the file set.
actions: Build every format in the deliverable list.
Run every quality check.
Deliver and confirm receipt.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

decision_points.question: Has the client chosen a direction, or asked for a new one?
decision_points.ifNew: Return to explore. A new direction is a new concept stage and is quoted.

decision_points.question: Are the agreed rounds used up?
decision_points.ifYes: Stop and quote. Do not absorb.

failure_conditions: Concepts presented before a direction was agreed
A revision round taken without being counted
Delivery of a file that fails one of the feature's own quality checks

wf.design_system.label: Building rules and reusable parts rather than a finished artefact
wf.design_system.trigger: The core identity this system derives from is approved.

stages.objective: Derive the system from what is already approved rather than inventing beside it.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Every part traces back to the approved core.

stages.objective: Prove it on real cases before anyone relies on it.
actions: Apply it to at least three unrelated real cases.
Include the awkward case, not three easy ones.
Fix what the awkward case breaks.
stages.validation: Three real cases produced correct results without special handling.

stages.objective: Write it down so someone else can use it correctly.
actions: Write the rules as rules, with examples.
State the limits explicitly.
Name every file.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Get the system agreed before things are built on it.
actions: Present with the three proofs.
Take one round of comments.
Deliver.
stages.validation: Client approval in writing.

decision_points.question: Did a real case need special handling?
decision_points.ifYes: Return to derive. A system with an exception on its first use is not finished.

failure_conditions: Documented without being proven on real cases
An example that only works with the example content

wf.design_asset.label: A finished item made from an established system
wf.design_asset.trigger: The system it is made from is approved, and the content for it exists.

stages.objective: Have everything before starting, so the work is not interrupted by a missing detail.
actions: Collect every input.
Query anything ambiguous now rather than assuming it.
stages.validation: Nothing on the input list is missing or guessed.

stages.objective: Make it.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Made from the brand's system, not designed beside it.

stages.objective: Find our own mistakes before the client does.
actions: Run every quality check on the feature.
Proofread names, numbers and dates against the client's own written source.
View at real size on a real device.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Get it approved within the agreed rounds.
actions: Send for approval.
Apply comments and count the round.
Stop at $feature.revisionRules.rounds.
stages.validation: Approval in writing, rounds within limit.

stages.objective: Export and hand over.
actions: Export every format in the deliverable list.
Deliver and confirm receipt.
stages.validation: Every deliverable opens.

decision_points.question: Is any input missing?
decision_points.ifYes: Stop and ask. Guessing a phone number is how a print run is wasted.

decision_points.question: Are the agreed rounds used up?

failure_conditions: Produced from a guessed input
Delivered without the checks having been run
A revision taken without being counted

wf.document.label: Writing a document that other people will work from
wf.document.trigger: Everything the document describes is approved.

stages.objective: Agree what the document covers before writing it.
actions: List the sections.
Confirm the list with whoever will use the document.
stages.validation: No section added later that should have been foreseen.

stages.objective: Write and lay out the document.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Every rule is shown as well as stated.

stages.objective: Check every value in the document against the file it came from.
actions: Cross-check every colour value, size, name and file reference against the source.
Fix the source or the document, and say which was wrong.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Deliver in the formats agreed.
actions: Export.
Deliver and confirm receipt.
stages.validation: Every deliverable opens and prints.

decision_points.question: Did a value in the document disagree with its source?
decision_points.ifYes: Fix both and record which was authoritative. A guideline that disagrees with the files is worse than none.

failure_conditions: A value in the document that no source file supports
A file reference that resolves to nothing

wf.production.label: A shoot — work that happens once, on a day, and cannot be repeated cheaply
wf.production.trigger: Date, location and shot list agreed, and access confirmed.

stages.objective: Agree exactly what has to come back from the day.
actions: Write the shot list with the client.
Confirm access, permits and every person appearing.
Agree the number of final items.
stages.output: An agreed shot list and call sheet
stages.validation: Every item on the list is achievable at that location on that day.

stages.objective: Capture the list, then capture beyond it.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Every item on the list has usable coverage before leaving.

stages.objective: Make the day unrepeatable-but-safe.
actions: Back up twice, to two places, before leaving the location.
Verify one backup by opening files from it.
stages.validation: A file has been opened from a backup, not merely copied to it.

stages.objective: Choose, then finish only what was chosen.
actions: Select against the shot list.
Present the selection for approval where the scope includes it.
Finish only the selected.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Deliver at every resolution in scope.
actions: Export at each resolution.
Deliver and confirm receipt.
stages.validation: Count delivered matches the count agreed.

decision_points.question: Is any shot-list item uncovered and the day ending?
decision_points.ifYes: Say so before leaving. A missing shot discovered in the edit is a second booking.

failure_conditions: Left a location with one copy of the material
Delivered fewer finals than agreed without saying so
An identifiable person with no written permission

wf.provision.label: Setting up an account or service that the client must end up owning
wf.provision.trigger: Scope signed and the client has decided who holds the account.
prerequisites: The client's billing details or their instruction to use ours

stages.objective: Find out what already exists before creating anything.
actions: Search for existing accounts, domains or profiles.
Recover rather than duplicate wherever recovery is possible.
stages.validation: No duplicate created where a recoverable original exists.

stages.objective: Create or claim, with the client as owner.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Ownership sits with the client; our role is delegated access.

stages.objective: Make it safe and make its renewal survive us.
actions: Enable two-factor with the client holding the second factor.
Turn on auto-renew where it applies.
Record expiry dates and account owners.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Prove it works from the client's side, not ours.
actions: Have the client log in themselves.
Confirm the service does the thing it was provisioned to do.
stages.validation: The client has logged in successfully at least once.

decision_points.question: Does an account already exist that we cannot access?
decision_points.ifYes: Recover it with the client before creating a second. A duplicate is a permanent problem.

decision_points.question: Is the client unwilling or unable to hold the account?
decision_points.ifYes: Record the exception in writing, with the date it should be revisited.

failure_conditions: An account left in our name without a written exception
Auto-renew off on anything with an expiry
A duplicate created beside a recoverable original

wf.build.label: Implementation work against an approved design or specification
wf.build.trigger: The design or specification is approved and its inputs are final.

stages.objective: Confirm the inputs are final before building on them.
actions: Check the design is approved, not merely shown.
Check the copy and images are final, not placeholder.
stages.validation: Nothing marked draft is being built against.

stages.objective: Build it.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Matches the approved design at every supported width.

stages.objective: Break it ourselves first.
actions: Run every quality check on the feature.
Try the failure path deliberately.
Check the console on every page.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Show it and take corrections.
actions: Send the staging address.
Take corrections as corrections; treat design changes as new scope.
stages.validation: Client has seen it on their own device.

decision_points.question: Is any input still a placeholder?
decision_points.ifYes: Do not build on it. Placeholder content is how a live site ships with lorem ipsum.

decision_points.question: Is a comment a correction or a design change?
decision_points.ifChange: Quote it. Absorbing design changes as corrections is how a fixed price stops being one.

failure_conditions: Built against unapproved design
A console error left on a page shown to the client
A failure path never tried

wf.verify.label: Checking work against a written list, and recording the result
wf.verify.trigger: The build is complete on staging.

stages.objective: Write down what will be checked before checking it.
actions: Write the check list from the feature's quality checks and the supported matrix.
Include the widths, languages and browsers by name.
stages.validation: The list names every width, language and browser in scope.

stages.objective: Run every check, including the boring ones.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.output: A completed check list with results
stages.validation: Every line has a result, including the ones that passed.

stages.objective: Fix what failed, or write down why it stands.
actions: Fix.
Re-run the failed check, not the whole list.
Where something will not be fixed, write why and get it accepted.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

decision_points.question: Is a failure being accepted rather than fixed?
decision_points.ifYes: It goes in writing to the client. An unfixed failure nobody was told about is a defect we chose.

failure_conditions: A check list line with no result
A failure fixed without the check being re-run
An accepted failure never told to the client

wf.release.label: Putting something live, where a mistake is visible to everyone
wf.release.trigger: Verification passed and the client has signed off on staging.

stages.objective: Know how to undo it before doing it.
actions: Identify the rollback and confirm it is available.
Take a backup of the current live state.
Pick a time when someone is available afterwards.
stages.validation: The rollback has been identified, not assumed.

stages.objective: Deploy.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: The deploy reported success.

stages.objective: Check the live thing, not the thing you deployed.
actions: Walk the live site page by page.
Confirm HTTPS, analytics and every form on the live address.
Watch for an hour before calling it done.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

decision_points.question: Does anything differ from staging?
decision_points.ifYes: Roll back first, diagnose second. Diagnosing in production is how a short outage becomes a long one.

failure_conditions: Deployed with no identified rollback
Live never checked independently of staging
Deployed at a time nobody could respond to a problem

wf.handover.label: Giving the client everything, so they could continue without us
wf.handover.trigger: Every item in scope is approved and live.

stages.objective: Collect everything, in a structure a stranger can navigate.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Folder names describe contents, not our internal process.

stages.objective: Write down what is in it and check the writing against the archive.
actions: Write the index.
Open every path in the index and confirm it resolves.
Remove anything the index does not account for.
stages.validation: Every index entry resolves to a file that exists.

stages.objective: Move ownership, not just copies.
actions: Transfer account ownership.
Hand over credentials through something that is not email.
Remove our standing access unless asked to keep it.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Get it confirmed by the person receiving it.
actions: Ask the client to open one file and log in to one account.
Get the confirmation in writing.
stages.validation: The client has confirmed, not merely been sent.

decision_points.question: Does the index reference something not in the archive?
decision_points.ifYes: Fix the archive, not the index. An index that quietly drops an entry hides the missing file.

failure_conditions: Archive sent without being opened by us first
An account still in our name
Credentials sent by email

wf.plan.label: Deciding what to do, and writing it down so it can be judged later
wf.plan.trigger: The period begins, or the previous period's report is in.

stages.objective: Read what already happened before deciding what happens next.
actions: Read the previous period's results where they exist.
Collect the client's own dates, launches and constraints.
stages.validation: The previous period's report has been read, where one exists.

stages.objective: Make the decisions the plan is made of.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Every element has a stated purpose, not just a slot.

stages.objective: Get it approved before anything is produced against it.
actions: Send for approval with enough time to answer.
Take one round of changes.
Fix the plan before production, not during it.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

decision_points.question: Has approval arrived in time to produce against it?
decision_points.ifNo: Say what will be late, before it is late.

failure_conditions: Production started against an unapproved plan
A plan with no measurable intent

wf.content.label: Making a piece of content — words, video, or both
wf.content.trigger: The plan it belongs to is approved.

stages.objective: Know what this piece is for before making it.
actions: Take the slot's stated purpose from the plan.
Confirm any factual detail with the client's own written source.
stages.validation: Every factual claim has a source.

stages.objective: Produce it.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Serves the stated purpose, and would be recognisable as this brand's.

stages.objective: Check it against the platform's rules and our own.
actions: Run the feature's quality checks.
Check length, ratio and policy for the destination.
Read the Arabic aloud where there is Arabic.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Get client approval within the agreed rounds.
actions: Send for approval.
Apply comments, counting the round.
Stop at $feature.revisionRules.rounds.
stages.validation: Approval recorded before scheduling.

decision_points.question: Is a factual claim unsourced?
decision_points.ifYes: Ask. Publishing an unsourced claim on the client's account is their problem, not ours, which is exactly why it is ours.

failure_conditions: Published without approval where approval was required
A claim published that no source supports
Arabic produced by translating the English

wf.recurring_service.label: Work that repeats on a cycle and is judged by whether the cycle held

stages.objective: Set the rhythm rather than reacting.
actions: Set the recurring times and the response window.
Name who covers it when the usual person cannot.
stages.validation: There is a named person for every slot in the cycle.

stages.objective: Do the work, on the cycle.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Nothing older than the agreed window is outstanding.

stages.objective: Confirm it actually happened, at the far end.
actions: Check the result on the platform itself, not in our own tool's status column.
Repeat anything that silently failed, the same day.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Leave a record the monthly report can be written from.
actions: Record what was done, what failed and what was escalated, with dates.
stages.validation: Every exception has a date and an owner.

decision_points.question: Did something fail silently?
decision_points.ifYes: Repeat it the same day and log it. A silent failure found at month end is a month of nothing.

failure_conditions: A cycle slot with no named person
A status trusted instead of verified at the platform
An escalation with no owner

wf.campaign.label: Building and launching paid advertising, where mistakes cost money per hour
wf.campaign.trigger: Strategy, audience, creative and tracking are all approved.

stages.objective: Check the expensive things before spending starts.
actions: Confirm tracking fires end to end.
Confirm every destination link opens the right page.
Confirm the budget figure against the client's written confirmation.
stages.validation: A test conversion has been seen, not assumed.

stages.objective: Build the campaign so it can be read later.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Structure isolates each variable being tested.

stages.objective: Have a second person look before it spends.
actions: Check budget, schedule, audience size, exclusions and links again.
Check every ad against the platform's policy.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Turn it on and watch the first hours.
actions: Enable.
Check delivery and spend rate within the first hours, not the next day.
Confirm the first conversions arrive where they should.
stages.validation: Delivering, spending at the agreed rate, conversions arriving.

decision_points.question: Is tracking unverified?
decision_points.ifYes: Do not launch. A campaign with no measurement is a donation.

decision_points.question: Is spend running above the agreed daily rate?

failure_conditions: Launched without a verified conversion
Budget different from the client's written figure
A destination link that 404s

wf.optimise.label: Changing a live thing on evidence, one variable at a time
wf.optimise.trigger: Enough data has accumulated to read.
prerequisites: A live campaign past its learning phase

stages.objective: Establish there is a signal before acting on it.
actions: Check the result count against the platform's own threshold.
Compare against the agreed target, not against yesterday.
stages.output: A read of the current state
stages.validation: The sample is large enough that the difference is not noise.

stages.objective: Make one change.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: Exactly one variable moved.

stages.objective: Write down the number that justified it.
actions: Log what changed, when, and the figure behind it.
Note what would make us reverse it.
stages.validation: The entry names a figure, not a feeling.

stages.objective: Let it settle before changing anything else.
actions: Wait out the learning period.
Compare against the recorded before-figure.
Reverse it if the reversal condition is met.
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

decision_points.question: Is the sample below the platform's learning threshold?
decision_points.ifYes: Change nothing. Most optimisation is reading noise confidently.

decision_points.question: Did the change make it worse?
decision_points.ifYes: Reverse it and log that too. An unlogged reversal is how the same change gets made again next quarter.

failure_conditions: More than one variable changed at once
A change with no recorded justification
A change made below the learning threshold

wf.report.label: Saying what happened, honestly, and deciding what changes

stages.objective: Take the numbers from the source, not from a dashboard we built.
actions: Export from each platform's own reporting.
Reconcile spend against the client's own invoice where money is involved.
stages.validation: Every figure traceable to a platform screen.

stages.objective: Say what the numbers mean, including when it is unflattering.
actions: $feature.executionSteps
stages.validation: The agreed target is stated and compared to, whichever way it went.

stages.objective: Turn the reading into a decision.
actions: State what changes next period, and why.
Where nothing changes, say that explicitly and why.
stages.output: A report with a decision in it
stages.validation: $feature.qualityChecks

stages.objective: Deliver it in time for it to be acted on.
actions: Send within the agreed window.
Where a call follows, send the report before the call, not during it.
stages.validation: Sent within the agreed number of days after period end.

decision_points.question: Did the period miss its target?
decision_points.ifYes: Say so in the first paragraph. A report that buries the miss is worth less than no report.

failure_conditions: A figure that no platform screen supports
A missed target not stated plainly
A report with no decision in it
Sent after the window without warning
